seo.title: What is a staging environment?
seo.description: A staging environment is a private copy of the live site where changes are tested before anyone outside the company sees them.

definition: A staging environment is a private copy of the live site where changes are tested before anyone outside the company sees them.
answerBlock: A staging environment is a private copy of the live site where changes are tested before anyone outside the company sees them. It runs the same code and a copy of the data, so a change behaves the same way it will in production. It is also where a backup restore is rehearsed.

body.heading: What is staging actually used for?
paragraphs: Reviewing content before it is published, testing platform and plugin updates, rehearsing migrations, and letting a client see a change in context rather than in a screenshot.

It has to be kept out of search results, or it competes with the live site for rankings. Password protection and a rule against indexing are both required, and a staging site that has leaked into an index is a familiar embarrassment.
Personal data needs care. A copy of production data means a copy of real customers, so it is either anonymised or protected exactly as carefully as production.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: Staging is what makes updates routine. Without it, every patch is applied to the live site and hoped for, which is how sites end up years behind and vulnerable.
It also shortens approval cycles: stakeholders sign off on the thing itself rather than on a description of it.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: Plugin and platform updates land on staging first, are checked against the main journeys, then go to production on a schedule, with a rehearsed restore if anything is wrong.

service.title: Website care plans
service.line: Patching, backups with a tested restore, monitoring and a fixed allowance of development hours.

terms.definition: A backup is a copy of the site and its database held somewhere else, and a restore is the rehearsed process of putting that copy back.
A content delivery network is a set of servers spread around the world that serve copies of your files from somewhere near each visitor.
DNS is the system that turns a domain name someone types into the address of the server that answers for it.
A TLS certificate is the file that lets a website prove who it is and encrypt the traffic between it and the visitor.
